exposure: Clinical presentation of microcephaly, hypotonia, and intracranial calcification
outcome: Intracranial calcifications (periventricular, subcortical white matter, basal ganglia)
Corpus callosal dysgenesis/thinning of corpus callosum with colpocephaly
Mild flattening of pontine belly with enlargement of retrocerebellar space
Multiple dysmorphic features (low-set ears, hypertelorism, thin upper lip, long philtrum)
cohort: The study describes a male neonate presenting with microcephaly, hypotonia, and intracranial calcification, along with his family history of a similar sibling.
finding: The study found that a male neonate presenting with microcephaly, hypotonia, and intracranial calcification, and a negative TORCH evaluation, was definitively diagnosed with Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome type 3 due to an RNASEH2C gene mutation.
